tasks.title: Create MarkdownRenderer component (web-optimized)
tasks.description: A component that takes a markdown string and renders it as beautifully styled HTML using react-markdown. This is the CORE of the entire redesign. Uses real CSS for pixel-perfect typography control.

implementation.component_signature: export function MarkdownRenderer({ content, isUser }: { content: string; isUser?: boolean })
implementation.approach: Use react-markdown's `components` prop to override each HTML element with a styled version. Each override is a simple function component that applies inline styles derived from tokens. This avoids needing a separate CSS file while keeping full control.

component_overrides._note: Each key is an HTML element that react-markdown renders. The override wraps it with inline styles. All colors reference tokens. When isUser=true, text colors become white.

ul._note: Remove default browser bullets — we render custom ones via li

li.render_pattern: For unordered lists: render a coral dot (●) as a ::before-like span, then the content. For ordered lists: use default numbering.

custom_bullet.element: <span> rendered before li children for ul lists
custom_bullet._note: Detect parent list type: if inside <ul>, prepend bullet span. If inside <ol>, let browser handle numbering. Pass ordered prop through context or check node.parentNode.tagName.

blockquote._note: This is the 'pro tip' / 'insight' box. Coral left border + very subtle coral tint.

code_inline._note: react-markdown renders inline code as <code> WITHOUT a <pre> wrapper. Detect this: if code element has no <pre> parent, it's inline.

styles.fontFamily: 'SF Mono', 'Fira Code', 'Fira Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

code_block._note: react-markdown renders code blocks as <pre><code>. Override the <pre> element for block styling.

styles.fontFamily: 'SF Mono', 'Fira Code', 'Fira Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

react_markdown_code_component_pattern._note: react-markdown passes code elements through a single `code` component override. Distinguish inline vs block by checking if the parent is <pre>. Here's the exact pattern:
react_markdown_code_component_pattern.code:
components={{ code({ node, inline, className, children, ...props }) { return inline ? {children} : {children}; }, pre({ children }) { return 
{children}
; } }}

implementation.user_mode_behavior: When isUser=true: all text colors (p, h1-h3, strong, li, etc.) switch to tokens.colors.text.inverse (#FFFFFF). Code blocks and blockquotes keep their own backgrounds. Bullet color stays coral (visible against navy). Create the styles object dynamically based on isUser prop — either compute at render or use a factory function: const getStyles = (isUser: boolean) => ({ ... }).

tasks.title: Create ThinkingIndicator with CSS animation
tasks.description: Animated thinking indicator with three pulsing dots and a tool activity subtitle. Uses CSS keyframe animation (more reliable on web than reanimated). Replaces the ugly ActivityIndicator + italic text.

implementation.component_signature: export function ThinkingIndicator({ thought }: { thought: string })

animation_approach.technique: CSS @keyframes injected via a <style> tag (or inline animation styles). On web, react-native-web's StyleSheet does NOT support @keyframes, so we inject a <style> element into the DOM on mount using useEffect.
animation_approach.keyframes_css: @keyframes pulseDot { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.3; transform: scale(1); } 50% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.4); } }
injection_pattern: style.textContent = `@keyframes pulseDot { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.3; transform: scale(1); } 50% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.4); } }`;

dots.render: Three <div> elements (or <View> with web style overrides) each 7px x 7px circles

animation_per_dot._note: 0.2s stagger between each dot creates the wave effect

implementation.web_style_application: Since we're on web, apply the animation CSS via the style attribute on each dot div: style={{ ...dotBaseStyles, animation: 'pulseDot 1.2s ease-in-out Xs infinite' }} where X is the stagger delay. Use Platform.OS === 'web' guard if needed, but since we're web-only for demo, can skip.

acceptance_criteria: Three dots pulse in a wave pattern (left → right, staggered by 0.2s each)
Animation is smooth and infinite (CSS-driven, no JS frame drops)
Tool activity text (thought prop) displays below dots in tertiary color
LedgerAvatar at 22px shows to the left
Feels alive — the wave pattern should be mesmerizing, not jarring
No console errors about @keyframes or style injection

tasks.title: Create ChatMessage component with entrance animation
tasks.description: Renders a single chat message with asymmetric design: user = compact right-aligned bubble, agent = editorial left-aligned content with coral accent border. CSS transition entrance animation.

implementation.component_signature: export function ChatMessage({ message, showAvatar }: { message: Message; showAvatar: boolean })
implementation.show_avatar_logic: The parent (chat.tsx) computes showAvatar: true when item.sender === 'agent' AND (index === 0 OR messages[index-1].sender === 'user'). Prevents avatar+name on every agent message.

entrance_animation.technique: CSS transition. On mount, set state from 'entering' to 'entered'. Apply styles based on state.
entrance_animation._note: Apply entranceStyle to the outermost wrapper div/View. The 200ms fade+slide is barely perceptible but removes the dead 'pop' feeling.

avatar_row._note_on_marginTop: 20px top margin creates clear visual separation between user question and agent response — makes it feel like a new 'section'

content_area._note_on_marginLeft: 11px ≈ half of 22px avatar, so the coral border aligns with the center of the avatar above

agent_message_design.background: NONE. Transparent. The coral left border IS the visual container. Content floats on the page background. This is the key design difference from the old bubble approach.

acceptance_criteria: User messages: right-aligned navy bubble, white text, rounded with flat bottom-right corner, max 75% width
Agent messages: NO bubble/background. Left-aligned. 2.5px coral left border. Markdown renders beautifully inside.
Avatar + 'Ledger' name only when showAvatar=true
Coral left border visually aligns below the avatar
20px top margin on avatar row creates clear separation between Q&A turns
Each message fades + slides up on mount (200ms CSS transition)
Agent content maxes at 90% width. User at 75%.
